entities.summary: The Younger Lady is the informal name given to an ancient Egyptian mummy discovered within tomb KV35 in the Valley of the Kings by archaeologist Victor Loret in 1898. The mummy also has been given the designation KV35YL and 61072, and currently resides in the Egyptian Museum in Cairo. Through DNA tests, this mummy was identified as the mother of the pharaoh Tutankhamun and a daughter of pharaoh Amenhotep III and his Great Royal Wife Tiye. Early speculation that this mummy was the remains of Nefertiti was argued to be incorrect, as nowhere is Nefertiti accorded the title "King's daughter" unless this mummy was in fact a cousin of Akhenaten and not a sister.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Younger Lady's identification as Tutankhamun's mother and Amenhotep III's daughter sheds new light on the royal family of ancient Egypt, providing a more accurate understanding of the succession crisis that led to Akhenaten's reign. This discovery has significant regional impact on our understanding of Egyptian history.
